core.title: Scaling Monosemanticity: Extracting Interpretable Features from Claude 3 Sonnet
Emotion Concepts and their Function in a Large Language Model
core.summary: Internal representations of emotion concepts are found, which encode the broad concept of a particular emotion and generalize across contexts and behaviors it might be linked to and causally influence the LLM's outputs, including Claude's preferences and its rate of exhibiting misaligned behaviors.

core.title: Jailbreak Distillation: Renewable Safety Benchmarking
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
core.summary: JBDistill addresses challenges in existing safety evaluation: the use of consistent evaluation prompts across models ensures fair comparisons and reproducibility, and requires minimal human effort to rerun the JBDistill pipeline and produce updated benchmarks, alleviating concerns on saturation and contamination.

core.title: SHADES: Towards a Multilingual Assessment of Stereotypes in Large Language Models
core.venue: North American Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: A new multi-lingual dataset designed for examining culturally-specific stereotypes that may be learned by LLMs, SHADES includes over 300 stereotypes from 37 regions, translated across 16 languages and annotated with multiple features to aid multilingual stereotype analysis.

core.title: Towards Uncovering How Large Language ModelsWork: An Interpretability Perspective
core.summary: This survey paper aims to cover the internal working mechanisms of LLM functionality through the lens of explainability, and explores how the insights gained can further enhance LLM performance through model editing, improve efficiency through pruning, and better align with human values.

core.title: Where Confabulation Lives: Latent Feature Discovery in LLMs
core.venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing

core.title: Sleepless Nights, Sugary Days: Creating Synthetic Users with Health Conditions for Realistic Coaching Agent Interactions
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: It is demonstrated that the proposed framework lays the foundation for efficient development of conversational agents through extensive, realistic, and grounded simulated interactions more accurately portray real human users with the same attributes compared to generic synthetic users not grounded in such attributes.

core.title: Rationales for Answers to Simple Math Word Problems Confuse Large Language Models
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics

core.title: Ask Again, Then Fail: Large Language Models’ Vacillations in Judgment
core.summary: A training-based framework is developed that teaches large language models to maintain their originally correct judgments through synthesized high-quality preference data and its ability to enhance the general capabilities of large language models is evaluated.

core.title: Understanding Inverse Scaling and Emergence in Multitask Representation Learning
core.venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics
core.summary: This work introduces “ task competition” to explain how tasks with dominant covariance eigen-spectrum emerge faster than others and shows that task competition can potentially explain the inverse scaling of certain tasks i.e. reduced test accuracy as the model grows.

core.title: The Capacity for Moral Self-Correction in Large Language Models
It's Not Easy Being Wrong: Evaluating Process of Elimination Reasoning in Large Language Models
core.summary: This work proposes PoE with COT, a new task where LLMs must reason toward incorrect options on multiple-choice questions, and shows that PoE consistently underperforms directly choosing the correct answer.

core.title: Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
core.summary: An iterated online mode of training, where preference models and RL policies are updated on a weekly cadence with fresh human feedback data, and a roughly linear relation between the RL reward and the square root of the KL divergence between the policy and its initialization is identified.

core.title: Language Models (Mostly) Know What They Know
core.summary: It is shown that larger models are well-calibrated on diverse multiple choice and true/false questions when they are provided in the right format and investigated whether models can be trained to predict P(IK), the probability that "I know" the answer to a question.

core.title: Red Teaming Language Models to Reduce Harms: Methods, Scaling Behaviors, and Lessons Learned
core.summary: It is found that the RLHF models are increasingly difficult to red team as they scale, and a flat trend with scale for the other model types is found.

core.title: Constitutional AI: Harmlessness from AI Feedback
core.summary: This work experiments with methods for training a harmless AI assistant through self-improvement, without any human labels identifying harmful outputs, and makes it possible to control AI behavior more precisely and with far fewer human labels.

core.title: Improving Coherence of Language Model Generation with Latent Semantic State
core.summary: Two procedures are introduced using explicit representations of world state as auxiliary supervision to improve LM coherence, in some cases providing the benefits of 1,000–9,000 training examples with only 500 state annotations.

core.title: Measuring Progress on Scalable Oversight for Large Language Models
core.summary: It is found that human participants who interact with an unreliable large-language-model dialog assistant through chat substantially outperform both the model alone and their own unaided performance, an encouraging sign that scalable oversight will be tractable to study with present models and bolster recent findings that large language models can productively assist humans with difficult tasks.

core.title: Toy Models of Superposition
core.summary: This paper provides a toy model where polysemanticity can be fully understood, arising as a result of models storing additional sparse features in "superposition" as a result of models storing additional sparse features in "superposition".

core.title: Predictability and Surprise in Large Generative Models
core.venue: Conference on Fairness, Accountability and Transparency
core.summary: This paper highlights a counterintuitive property of large-scale generative models, which have a paradoxical combination of predictable loss on a broad training distribution, and unpredictable specific capabilities, inputs, and outputs, and analyzed how these conflicting properties combine to give model developers various motivations for deploying these models, and challenges that can hinder deployment.

core.title: Scaling Laws and Interpretability of Learning from Repeated Data
core.summary: It is shown that data repetition disproportionately damages copying and internal structures associated with generalization, such as induction heads, providing a possible mechanism for the shift from generalization to memorization.

core.title: In-context Learning and Induction Heads
core.summary: It is found that induction heads develop at precisely the same point as a sudden sharp increase in in-context learning ability, visible as a bump in the training loss.

core.title: Discovering Language Model Behaviors with Model-Written Evaluations
core.venue: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
core.summary: This work automatically generates evaluations with LMs, finding some of the first examples of inverse scaling in RL from Human Feedback (RLHF), where more RLHF makes LMs worse.

core.title: A General Language Assistant as a Laboratory for Alignment
core.summary: This work studies simple baseline techniques and evaluations and finds that the benefits from modest interventions increase with model size, generalize to a variety of alignment evaluations, and do not compromise the performance of large models.

core.title: Concrete Problems in AI Safety
core.summary: A list of five practical research problems related to accident risk, categorized according to whether the problem originates from having the wrong objective function, an objective function that is too expensive to evaluate frequently, or undesirable behavior during the learning process, are presented.

core.title: MED-OMIT: Extrinsically-Focused Evaluation of Omissions in Medical Summarization
core.summary: This work proposes MED-OMIT, a new omission benchmark for medical summarization, which leverages LLM prompt-based approaches which categorize the importance of facts and cluster them as supporting or negating evidence to the diagnosis.

core.title: Reliability Scales Inversely: Bigger Models Compound Mistakes Faster via a Hidden Auto-Regressive Risk Regime
core.summary: Under scaling, the knowledge gap falls while knowledge degradation grows 11 – 39 × and at a fabrication, felt uncertainty H ( p M ) re-laxes quickly while oracle-referenced risk persists up to 17 × longer, leaving a confident-but-precarious risk regime that bridges consecutive fabrications.
